answer: Treat trust like water flowing across a meadow from a few known springs: reputation spreads only along real trade edges between agents, and each hop splits it thinner. An atlas of these edges shows fake clusters as islands joined to the honest graph by just a handful of links, so they receive almost no trust. To reach the summit of influence, an attacker must earn many genuine trades with honest agents for every fake, paying real work and fees that grow with each identity.
